fixes.explanation: Wicked is the word, friend. Verse 3 says Er, Judah's firstborn, “…was wicked in the sight of the LORD. So the LORD put him to death.” That's a heavy line. I think this one hurts.
Tamar it is. Verse 4 says, “Tamar, Judah’s daughter-in-law, bore to him Perez and Zerah.” So the first three sons came by Bath-shua the Canaanite, and these two came by Tamar.
True, friend. Er, Onan and Shelah came by Bath-shua (verse 3), and Perez and Zerah came by Tamar. Verse 4 wraps it up: “Judah had five sons in all.” Three and two make five.
Jesse. Verse 12 says “…Obed was the father of Jesse.” And the list names seven sons of Jesse, with David at the end of that line. We just walked up to the front door of David's house.
Ozem is sixth, right before the last spot. Verse 15 says “Ozem sixth, and David seventh.” So Ozem sits one place ahead of David.
Nephew is it. Verse 16 says Zeruiah is David's sister, and Joab is her son. So David is Joab's uncle, and Joab is David's nephew. Joab ends up leading David's army (2 Samuel 8:16).
Amasa is the one. Verse 17 says, “Abigail was the mother of Amasa, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.” Since Abigail is David's sister (verse 16), Amasa is another nephew of David's.

Hiram was a king who sent cedar logs and builders to David (2 Samuel 5:11). He's a real king in David's story, but he's not Maacah's father. Verse 2 names Talmai of Geshur for that. Good king guess, friend.

Amnon is David's firstborn, born in Hebron to Ahinoam of Jezreel (verse 1). Bathsheba's four were born in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan and Solomon (verse 5). Amnon isn't among them. Watch the cities and the mothers, and the list sorts them for you.
Merab was Saul's older daughter (1 Samuel 18:17). She isn't named in this list. Verse 9 says, “And Tamar was their sister.” Lots of daughters in David's world, so the names can blur together.

Josiah, friend. Verse 14 closes the run with “Amon his son, and Josiah his son.” After that, the list moves on to Josiah's own sons in verse 15. Those four are Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah and Shallum.
Captive is the word. Verse 17 says “The descendants of Jeconiah the captive…” Jeremiah 24:1 tells of Jeconiah being carried away to Babylon.

The verse doesn't call Jeconiah a prophet. It says, “The descendants of Jeconiah the captive…” Jeremiah 24:1 says he was carried away to Babylon. The text gives him a different title, and that title is captive.
